hardRules: Use at least one primary source.
Use the original announcement or release time for recency. A refreshed page, crawler date, repost, or later page update does not make an older story new.
Do not cover a story already present in history or the current story file.
Do not publish rumours, leaks, predictions, or unverified benchmark claims.

The core of every story must be a new technology, model, capability, developer tool, hardware release, research result, scientific discovery, benchmark-relevant technical advance, robotics advance, infrastructure change, security finding, or meaningful open-source release.

Do not select hiring, recruitment, fellowships, training academies, educational cohorts, job programs, grants, workforce-reskilling initiatives, or company staffing announcements unless the actual news is a substantial new technology or research result.
Exclude routine partnerships, funding announcements, customer wins, executive commentary, and generic business expansion unless they reveal a concrete technical development.
Prefer stories with a clear technical delta that can be shown visually: before versus after, a measurable result, a new workflow, a new capability, or a discovery.
Explain what changed, why it matters, and any material limitation.
When citing company-reported benchmarks, make the attribution clear and avoid presenting them as independent verification.
Do not exaggerate the source or introduce claims the source does not support.
Use clear, fast language for a technical but broad audience.
